key_insight: Deep neural network intensity estimators achieve structure-adaptive convergence guarantees for covariate-driven Poisson processes, even when the true intensity can vanish.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports flexible event-rate modeling under changing external conditions while reducing dimensionality burdens when compositional or manifold structure is present.
method: Estimate covariate-dependent intensity by nonparametric maximum likelihood.
Derive an oracle inequality using covariate-averaged Hellinger distance without a positive lower bound on intensity.
Use DNN estimators to exploit compositional structure and adapt to low-dimensional event-space manifolds.
evidence_signal: Simulations favor DNN estimators over kernels in most settings, and Allen Brain Observatory neural-spiking data show better held-out log-likelihood than a conditional kernel estimator.
watch_item: Performance gains are not universal: manifold kernels remain competitive in some simulation designs.
paper_title: Nonparametric Intensity Estimation for Covariate-Driven Poisson Processes Using Deep Learning
